facts.text: Whitesburg was founded in 1842 on land offered by Stephen Hiram Hogg to become the county seat.
Before becoming Whitesburg, the town was called Summit City, a name that reflected its lofty position in the mountains.
The weekly newspaper The Mountain Eagle, started by Nehemiah Webb in 1907, has been owned by the Gish family of Letcher County since 1956.
Walking through downtown Whitesburg, you’ll see compact streets and historic civic buildings that map the town’s evolution over time.
Whitesburg sits amid rolling hills and forested ridges, offering dramatic mountain views from almost every corner of town.
Historic photographs and public records in Whitesburg let visitors compare 19th‑century streetscapes with today’s landscape, revealing how the town has changed.
